stdout: === A. THE TEAM THAT ADOPTED AI BEFORE ANYONE WROTE RULES ===
0/110 (0%) · Do not publish AI-drafted work yet

Blocked on: Tools named, by task; The never-in-a-prompt list is written down; Training-on-inputs setting verified, not assumed; A named human reviewer; Figures are added by a person, not asked for. These are the checks that sit between the draft and the publish button.
failed checks:

- Tools named, by task — No tool named for: Research and summarising; First drafts — blog, email, social; Editing, proofing, shortening; Images and video; Code on the marketing site; Customer or revenue data analysis
- Each approved tool says who may use it — Every row has a person against it
- The never-in-a-prompt list is written down — Treat every prompt as though it may be read by someone outside the company, because it may be
- Training-on-inputs setting verified, not assumed — Consumer tiers often train on inputs and the default is rarely the safe one. Check it, write the answer down, re-check it when the plan changes
- A named human reviewer — "the team" is not a name. Accountability that is not a name is not accountability
- Reviewer's name is recorded somewhere durable — The doc, the ticket or the CMS field — somewhere it survives the week
- All four review questions in use — The four questions are what the reviewer is accountable for
- Figures are added by a person, not asked for — Ask AI for the argument, not the statistics. A model generates plausible citations, not retrieved ones
- Disclosure line decided — Disclose where the reader's judgement depends on who wrote it; routine drafting help needs no more disclosure than a spellchecker
- Policy has an owner and a next review date — A policy nobody owns is a document, not a policy
=== B. THE SAME TEAM, POLICY ADOPTED ===
Tools are named, the prompt line is drawn, a person signs, and figures come from documents.
=== CITATION CHECK (section 5) ===
"35% of failed startups cited no market need" — citeable
"Strong positioning makes the next round 30% faster" — not citeable
- No document title.
- No document date.
- Incomplete sample: it needs how many, of what, measured when.
- Publisher index, tag or category page — a citation resolves to one document
- Nobody has opened this document. Add figures one at a time, each from a document you opened yourself.
If a claim needs a number you cannot find, the claim is wrong — not under-researched.
=== DRAFT SWEEP ===
figures found: 30%, 35% — not ready
- Figure with no citation attached: 30%. Ask AI for the argument, not the statistics.
- Published under a named person's byline without that person reading and approving it.
- Disclosure needed: the reader's judgement here depends on who wrote it.
- No named reviewer. Nothing AI-drafted publishes without one.
=== THE FIVE RULES ===
01  AI drafts. People decide and sign.
No exceptions, no "it was only a social post".
02  Use the tools on the list.
Anything else needs approval first.
03  Nothing confidential goes into a prompt.
Customers, pricing, NDAs, credentials — none of it.
04  Ask for the argument, not the statistics.
Add every figure yourself, from a document you opened.
05  A named person reviews before publish.
Their name goes somewhere that survives the week.
